title: Lucky Millinder's coffin-like sleeping bus
summary: Lucky had a bus converted into beds too low to stand in, which the band rebelled against.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: You were just saying that in plain economics, that was one way to be able to get gas, huh?
Yeah, that was the only way we were able to get gas -- by the bus.
Do you have any particular stories about that?

Well, I'll tell you. Lucky got the bright idea, because we were having problems in the different towns that we were playing in, of getting rooms. So, Lucky goes and buys a bus and had the bus remodeled on the inside with beds in it, but there was only one thing wrong with this bus -- we couldn't stand up. We had to lay down all the time. And, so this lasted for about three months.
Why did you have to lay down all the time?

Because we couldn't stand up. It was a row of beds inside of the bus for you to lay down, and that was the only thing you could do in there, was lay down. When you took your clothes off, you had to lay down -- you could not stand up. There was no height in the bus, because on the top of the bus, there was another row of beds.
On both sides of the bus, so you couldn't stand up.
Oh, now I get the picture.

So we had to lay down all the time. So after about the third month, the whole band rebelled, and said we weren't gonna ride in this bus any more, that he would have to find another bus; that we weren't gonna ride in that thing any more. It looked like a Hearse -- it was so big and funny looking.

And so he had to go out and hire a regular bus for us to ride in, although on many nights, we had to sleep in the bus because we weren't able to get any rooms, you know? All the rooms in the different towns were taken up by the soldiers.
Uh huh. Let's go back to the '60s, unless you have something else to say, elaborate on the Lucky Millinder era. We have plenty of time to do it.
